name: John Marshall
bio: Liverpool wine-merchant's son who went up to New College, Oxford, on a Classics scholarship intending Holy Orders, met Ned Warren in his third year (1884), and after Warren's five-year wooing gave up church, a Fellowship path and Liverpool to join him in November 1889 - thereafter co-head of the Lewes House collecting operation, whose eye supplied the classical collections of Boston and, from 1906, the Metropolitan Museum as its Rome-based purchasing agent. He and Warren called each other 'Puppy'; Burdett described the pair 'pacing arm-in-arm on the lawn at Lewes House' as 'replicas of each other'. He married Warren's cousin Mary Bliss on 5 November 1907 - 'Neither love nor sex had anything to do with the union' per Sox - and after her death in 1925 shared his old Rome flat with Warren again. He died there in February 1928 with Warren beside him - his last words, in Warren's account, 'good-bye Puppy' - and is buried at Bagni di Lucca with Mary and Warren, under a plain Grecian urn.
bio_sources: Liverpool family, wine-merchant father: Sox (1991) p. 39
Liverpool College, Classics scholarship to New College, met Warren 1884 ('It was in his third year at New College (1884) that he met Ned.'), Merton Fellowship path abandoned: Sox p. 40
Joined Warren: 'By November 1889, "the man of his choice" was at Ned's side.' - Sox p. 44
Met purchasing agent from Robinson's 1905-06 offer; Rome flat 'made possible by Ned's generosity': Sox pp. 77-78, 107

Died: 'She died there in 1925, and Marshall in Rome in February, 1928.' - Sox p. viii; Portland newspaper: 'passed away in the latter country in February, 1928' - p. 130; Warren's account of the night, pp. 126-127

British School at Rome, John Marshall Archive catalogue (archive.bsr.ac.uk, resource 65); Guido Petruccioli, 'Introduction', Ancient Art and its Commerce in Early Twentieth-Century Europe (Archaeopress, 2022), p. 1 - birth year
bio_note: Sox states no birth date or year for Marshall in the pages read (text search for '1862' returns nothing); the enlarged Bagni di Lucca monument carries the three names 'with their birth and death dates' (p. 130) but Sox does not print them - born stays null. Death not sharpened past the month: Sox's narration gives 'February, 1928'; Warren's first-person account has Marshall dying at 'five minutes past one' in the night after 'the evening of the 15th'. 'Johnny' is Warren's and the circle's regular name for him; 'Puppy' was mutual (Marshall writes 'Puppy dear' to Warren, pp. 64-65; Warren signs 'Your Puppy', p. 107). (1) The British School at Rome's archival catalogue for the John Marshall Archive - the repository that holds his papers (BSR Archive & Special Collections, ArchivesSpace resource 65, fonds 1900-1928, archive.bsr.ac.uk) - whose biographical note reads 'John Marshall (1862-1928) was a connoisseur of Classical art and a cultivated intellectual.' (2) Guido Petruccioli, 'Introduction', in Ancient Art and its Commerce in Early Twentieth-Century Europe (Archaeopress, 2022), p. 1, read in the publisher's own sample PDF: 'John Marshall (1862-1928) - not to be confused with the homonymous (and far more notorious) American statesman John Marshall (1755-1835) or the British archaeologist John Hubert Marshall (1876-1958) - is known only to a few people.' This closes the gap Sox left: Sox reports that the Bagni di Lucca monument carries 'their birth and death dates' (p. 130) without transcribing them. Death-date conflict, reported not resolved - died stays {y:1928, m:2}: Wikipedia's 'John Marshall (died 1928)' opens '15 February 1928' but attaches no citation to that date (its listed references are Streitmatter, Outlaw Marriages, and De Puma, Etruscan Art in the Metropolitan Museum of Art); Sox's repo text has Warren's first-person account of Marshall retiring on 'the evening of the 15th' and dying at 'five minutes past one' in the night, which points to the small hours of 16 February; BSR and Petruccioli give the year only.
